rationales: J.J. Thomson was not British chemist by profession; he was a physicist.
He was not an economist.
He was a British physicist who discovered the electron.
He was not a dentist.
The first period does not begin with an alkali metal.
The first period does not begin with an alkaline earth metal.
The first period does not begin with a noble gas.
Hydrogen is the first element in the first period.
A large electronegativity difference, conventionally above about 1.7, indicates an ionic bond.
Covalent bonds generally form when the electronegativity difference is smaller.
A coordinate covalent bond involves a shared pair donated by one atom, not simply this electronegativity difference.
Metallic bonding involves metal atoms and is not classified by this electronegativity rule.
N₂ has a complete octet around each nitrogen atom.
H₂O has complete valence shells around its atoms.
NH₃ has a complete octet around nitrogen.
BF₃ is electron deficient because boron has only six electrons around it in the molecule.
Tin’s transition temperature is not 12.2 °C.
The transition temperature of white tin to gray tin is about 13.2 °C.
14.2 °C is not the accepted transition temperature of tin.
15.2 °C is not the accepted transition temperature of tin.
Carbon dioxide is dissolved in the soft drink and is a solute.
Salt, if present, is a solute rather than the solvent.
Water is the solvent in a soft drink.
Sugar is dissolved in the drink and is a solute.
Chalk in water is generally a suspension, not a colloid.
Milk of magnesia is generally treated as a suspension, not a definite colloid example.
Paint is a colloid, with pigment particles dispersed in a liquid.
Jelly is a colloid, specifically a gel, so this is also a correct example.
32 is not the molecular mass of CO₂.
Molecular mass is expressed in atomic mass units, but CO₂ has a mass of 44 amu.
44 g is a molar mass unit, not the molecular mass of one molecule.
CO₂ has molecular mass 12 + 2(16) = 44 amu.
Benzene does not ionize to produce ions in solution, so it is a non-electrolyte.
Sodium hydroxide dissociates into ions and is an electrolyte.
Sodium chloride dissociates into ions and is an electrolyte.
Sulphuric acid ionizes in water and is an electrolyte.
Lithium is the least electropositive among these listed alkali metals.
Sodium is less electropositive than potassium and rubidium.
Potassium is less electropositive than rubidium.
Electropositivity increases down the group, making rubidium the most electropositive listed.
The molar mass of H₂SO₄ is 2(1) + 32 + 4(16) = 98 g/mol, so one mole has a mass of 98 g.
96 g is less than the molar mass of H₂SO₄.
94 g is less than the molar mass of H₂SO₄.
92 g is less than the molar mass of H₂SO₄.
The L shell has a capacity of more than two electrons.
For the L shell, n = 2, so its maximum capacity is 2n² = 8 electrons.
Eighteen electrons is the maximum capacity of the M shell, not the L shell.
Thirty-two electrons is the maximum capacity of the N shell, not the L shell.
Fluorine is the most electronegative halogen, not the least.
Chlorine is more electronegative than iodine.
Electronegativity decreases down the group, so iodine is the least electronegative listed halogen.
Bromine is more electronegative than iodine.
H₂SO₄ is a molecular compound with covalent bonds.
NaCl is an ionic compound.
KOH is primarily ionic between K⁺ and OH⁻, though the hydroxide ion has a covalent bond.
CaCl₂ is an ionic compound.
The M shell has more than one subshell.
The M shell does not have only two subshells.
For n = 3, the M shell has three subshells: s, p, and d.
Four subshells belong to the N shell, where n = 4.
